title: Apple should be ashamed of its hostile App Store rating system

Articles index
Jeff Johnson (My apps, PayPal.Me, Mastodon)

July 29 2026

I could have terminated the title of this blog post with “App Store” but wanted to talk about something specific that came up for me today: App Store user ratings and reviews. This subject is related to yesterday’s blog post No, you curate the App Store. Despite the fact that Apple employees privately review every version of every app before developers can publish to the App Store, supposedly ensuring the quality of apps, verifying that they do what they claim to do, Apple nonetheless also relies on App Store users to rate and review apps. You might wonder how an Apple-reviewed, Apple-approved app could still earn one-star ratings. On the other hand, some of these one-star ratings are undeserved, unfair.

When the App Store opened 18 years ago, it was a carbon copy of the iTunes Music Store designed to sell 99 cent songs. In fact, the iPhone App Store was included with iTunes for Mac. This song-inspired design had many unfortunate consequences for the software market, such as the chart-driven race to the bottom. You might forgive Apple for throwing together a system hastily: after all, when the iPhone itself was introduced the previous year, it did not support third-party native apps. Instead, web apps were the “sweet solution” defended by Steve Jobs, though most other people soured on the idea. In any case, that was two Apple CEOs ago, with John Ternus now ascending to the office. The App Store has grown enormously over time, yet in a number of important ways it remains the same old ill-conceived clone of the iTunes Music Store, to the detriment of App Store users and developers.

It ought to be obvious how the song and software markets differ:

  1. Price. Songs in the iTunes Music Store were mostly 99 cents or near that price, whereas the price of apps in the App Store varies dramatically. Apple’s own Final Cut Pro in the Mac App Store is $299.99.
  2. Purchasing. Songs do not have In-Song Purchase. They’re all upfront paid. Although some old-school developers such as myself stubbornly cling to the upfront paid business model for apps, the App Store incentivizes In-App Purchases, and the majority of apps follow Apple’s incentives.
  3. Quality. A song “just works,” and if for some reason it refuses to play, that’s the fault of Apple and iTunes rather than a “bug” written in the song by the musician. A song downloaded from the iTunes Music Store does one and only one thing: play audio. Songs don’t have multiple features, options, and workflows like apps do. If a song displeases you, that’s not a bug either; music is mainly a matter of personal taste.
  4. Support. Software requires technical support from the developer. Songs do not require technical support from the musician. You generally can’t contact the musician. Maybe Ringo Starr will answer your fan mail decades later.
  5. Safety. The iTunes Music Store has no malware or scams. The greatest danger would be explicit lyrics. The musicians have already been curated by the record labels, so Apple doesn’t need to review songs before publishing them. To my knowledge, the iTunes Music Store does not accept amateur submissions from the public. In contrast, any unknown person in the world with $99 to pay for the Apple Developer Program can submit apps to the App Store.

The anonymous crowdsourced rating and review system was designed for songs, where the only thing that matters is personal musical taste. Songs are entertainment, not utilitarian. This system is horrible when applied to apps. Below is a one-star review that I discovered today—App Store developers must check manually for reviews because Apple fails to send us email notifications, as I mentioned in my blog post Small ways the App Store could be improved for developers—complaining that my app requested a rating… like the majority of other apps in the App Store!

Edit: Some readers, for example on Hacker News (sigh), are assuming way too much from the above screenshot, without having used my app. I posted this review because it’s recent, not because it’s typical. In fact it’s atypical. I can’t remember anyone else ever reviewing my rating request. Overall, my app is highly rated and well reviewed. The reviewer in this case uses the word “nag,” but my app doesn’t have a nag screen. There’s a nonmodal button that does not interrupt your use of the app. My complaint in this blog post is about Apple’s system, not about my own reviews.

Imagine if a professional writer for the tech news media submitted this app review to their editor for publication. The writer would likely be fired for incompetence. Yet Apple allows reviews like this to be published to the App Store. Also today, a fellow App Store developer on social media posted a screenshot of one-star review that their app received for a feature request:

Neither of these reviews talk about the actual features of the app, whether they work or how well they work. The reviews are irrationally nitpicky, choosing one quibble and making the entire review about that. Somehow the apps deserve an overall one-star rating based on that one factor? The fundamental problem is that in general, App Store users are not qualified by experience or temperament to write software reviews. They’re rank amateurs, not professionals. Software deserves much better than this. Some App Store users even abuse the review system for technical support purposes, instead of contacting support to ask their question, but it’s practically impossible to have a back-and-forth conversation with users in the App Store review and developer response, for example if I need more information from the user. The system was definitely not designed for that!

Indie developers can’t win in the App Store. Since we’re mostly unknown to the public, we need positive App Store ratings and reviews for our apps to encourage purchases. If we don’t request ratings from all users, then the self-initiated ratings tend to be disproportionately people with a complaint rather than satisfied users. The enlightened users recognize our dilemma, but there are also vigilante users like the one above who seems determined to punish all ratings requests, and as an unintended consequence, put indie developers out of business. Apple could mitigate this problem by emailing App Store customers at some point after purchase with a request to rate the app, so that app developers don’t need to request reviews. Indeed, if ratings requests were initiated by Apple, then Apple could go as far as to ban developer-initiated ratings requests in the App Store. Unfortunately, Apple doesn’t seem interested in mitigating any problems with the App Store. Apple doesn’t even admit that the rating and review system is problematic.

Should you even trust anonymous crowdsourced ratings and reviews? The ratings and reviews for upfront paid apps are probably mostly honest, albeit often poorly written. Developers could write or buy fake reviews, but in volume that would become quite costly. For apps that are free to download, on the other hand, anyone in the world can rate and review the app. This frequently leads to fraud. Nefarious services exist that can sell fake ratings and reviews in volume to unscrupulous App Store developers. Apple claims to prevent App Store fraud, but Apple seems to be about as effective at stopping fake ratings and reviews as it is at stopping scam apps from appearing in the App Store. In other words, not very effective.

In 2026, we’re long overdue for Apple to “think different” about App Store user ratings and reviews. What I see from Apple here is nothing except shameful complacency.

Jeff Johnson (My apps, PayPal.Me, Mastodon)

sentences.en: My complaint in this blog post is about Apple’s system, not about my own reviews.
sentences.zh: 我在这篇博文中抱怨的是苹果的系统，而不是我自己的评论。

blocks.html_en: Imagine if a professional writer for the tech news media submitted this app review to their editor for publication. The writer would likely be fired for incompetence. Yet Apple allows reviews like this to be published to the App Store. Also today, a fellow App Store developer on social media posted a screenshot of one-star review that their app received for a feature request:

sentences.en: Imagine if a professional writer for the tech news media submitted this app review to their editor for publication.
sentences.zh: 想象一下，如果科技新闻媒体的专业作家将此应用程序评论提交给他们的编辑以供出版。

sentences.en: The writer would likely be fired for incompetence.
sentences.zh: 作者可能会因无能而被解雇。

sentences.en: Yet Apple allows reviews like this to be published to the App Store.
sentences.zh: 然而苹果允许这样的评论发布到应用商店。

sentences.en: Also today, a fellow App Store developer on social media posted a screenshot of one-star review that their app received for a feature request:
sentences.zh: 同样在今天，一位 App Store 开发者在社交媒体上发布了他们的应用收到的功能请求一星评论的屏幕截图：

blocks.html_en: Neither of these reviews talk about the actual features of the app, whether they work or how well they work. The reviews are irrationally nitpicky, choosing one quibble and making the entire review about that. Somehow the apps deserve an overall one-star rating based on that one factor? The fundamental problem is that in general, App Store users are not qualified by experience or temperament to write software reviews. They’re rank amateurs, not professionals. Software deserves much better than this. Some App Store users even abuse the review system for technical support purposes, instead of contacting support to ask their question, but it’s practically impossible to have a back-and-forth conversation with users in the App Store review and developer response, for example if I need more information from the user. The system was definitely not designed for that!

sentences.en: Neither of these reviews talk about the actual features of the app, whether they work or how well they work.
sentences.zh: 这些评论都没有谈论该应用程序的实际功能，无论它们是否有效或工作得如何。

sentences.en: The reviews are irrationally nitpicky, choosing one quibble and making the entire review about that.
sentences.zh: 这些评论是非理性的挑剔，选择一个狡辩并对此进行整个评论。

sentences.en: Somehow the apps deserve an overall one-star rating based on that one factor?
sentences.zh: 不知何故，基于这一因素，这些应用程序应该获得整体一星评级吗？

sentences.en: The fundamental problem is that in general, App Store users are not qualified by experience or temperament to write software reviews.
sentences.zh: 根本问题在于，总体而言，App Store 用户无论从经验还是气质上都没有资格撰写软件评论。

sentences.en: They’re rank amateurs, not professionals.
sentences.zh: 他们是业余爱好者，而不是专业人士。

sentences.en: Software deserves much better than this.
sentences.zh: 软件值得比这更好的东西。

sentences.en: Some App Store users even abuse the review system for technical support purposes, instead of contacting support to ask their question, but it’s practically impossible to have a back-and-forth conversation with users in the App Store review and developer response, for example if I need more information from the user.
sentences.zh: 一些App Store用户甚至出于技术支持的目的滥用审核系统，而不是联系支持人员提出问题，但实际上不可能在App Store审核和开发人员响应中与用户进行来回对话，例如，如果我需要用户提供更多信息。

sentences.en: The system was definitely not designed for that!
sentences.zh: 该系统绝对不是为此设计的！

blocks.html_en: Indie developers can’t win in the App Store. Since we’re mostly unknown to the public, we need positive App Store ratings and reviews for our apps to encourage purchases. If we don’t request ratings from all users, then the self-initiated ratings tend to be disproportionately people with a complaint rather than satisfied users. The enlightened users recognize our dilemma, but there are also vigilante users like the one above who seems determined to punish all ratings requests, and as an unintended consequence, put indie developers out of business. Apple could mitigate this problem by emailing App Store customers at some point after purchase with a request to rate the app, so that app developers don’t need to request reviews. Indeed, if ratings requests were initiated by Apple, then Apple could go as far as to ban developer-initiated ratings requests in the App Store. Unfortunately, Apple doesn’t seem interested in mitigating any problems with the App Store. Apple doesn’t even admit that the rating and review system is problematic.

sentences.en: Indie developers can’t win in the App Store.
sentences.zh: 独立开发者无法在 App Store 中获胜。

sentences.en: Since we’re mostly unknown to the public, we need positive App Store ratings and reviews for our apps to encourage purchases.
sentences.zh: 由于我们大多不为公众所知，因此我们需要对我们的应用程序进行正面的 App Store 评级和评论来鼓励购买。

sentences.en: If we don’t request ratings from all users, then the self-initiated ratings tend to be disproportionately people with a complaint rather than satisfied users.
sentences.zh: 如果我们不要求所有用户进行评分，那么自发评分的人往往会不成比例地是有抱怨的用户，而不是满意的用户。

sentences.en: The enlightened users recognize our dilemma, but there are also vigilante users like the one above who seems determined to punish all ratings requests, and as an unintended consequence, put indie developers out of business.
sentences.zh: 开明的用户认识到我们的困境，但也有像上面那位这样的私刑用户，他们似乎决心惩罚所有评级请求，并产生意想不到的结果，使独立开发者破产。

sentences.en: Apple could mitigate this problem by emailing App Store customers at some point after purchase with a request to rate the app, so that app developers don’t need to request reviews.
sentences.zh: 苹果可以通过在购买后的某个时候向 App Store 客户发送电子邮件，要求对应用程序进行评分来缓解这个问题，这样应用程序开发人员就不需要请求评论。

sentences.en: Indeed, if ratings requests were initiated by Apple, then Apple could go as far as to ban developer-initiated ratings requests in the App Store.
sentences.zh: 事实上，如果评级请求是由苹果发起的，那么苹果甚至可以禁止开发者在 App Store 中发起评级请求。

sentences.en: Unfortunately, Apple doesn’t seem interested in mitigating any problems with the App Store.
sentences.zh: 不幸的是，苹果似乎对缓解应用商店的任何问题不感兴趣。

sentences.en: Apple doesn’t even admit that the rating and review system is problematic.
sentences.zh: 苹果甚至不承认评级和评论系统存在问题。

blocks.html_en: Should you even trust anonymous crowdsourced ratings and reviews? The ratings and reviews for upfront paid apps are probably mostly honest, albeit often poorly written. Developers could write or buy fake reviews, but in volume that would become quite costly. For apps that are free to download, on the other hand, anyone in the world can rate and review the app. This frequently leads to fraud. Nefarious services exist that can sell fake ratings and reviews in volume to unscrupulous App Store developers. Apple claims to prevent App Store fraud, but Apple seems to be about as effective at stopping fake ratings and reviews as it is at stopping scam apps from appearing in the App Store. In other words, not very effective.

sentences.en: Should you even trust anonymous crowdsourced ratings and reviews?
sentences.zh: 您是否应该相信匿名的众包评级和评论？

sentences.en: The ratings and reviews for upfront paid apps are probably mostly honest, albeit often poorly written.
sentences.zh: 预付费应用程序的评级和评论可能大多是诚实的，尽管通常写得不好。

sentences.en: Developers could write or buy fake reviews, but in volume that would become quite costly.
sentences.zh: 开发商可以撰写或购买虚假评论，但如果数量过多，成本将变得相当高。

sentences.en: For apps that are free to download, on the other hand, anyone in the world can rate and review the app.
sentences.zh: 另一方面，对于免费下载的应用程序，世界上任何人都可以对应用程序进行评分和评论。

sentences.en: This frequently leads to fraud.
sentences.zh: 这常常导致欺诈。

sentences.en: Nefarious services exist that can sell fake ratings and reviews in volume to unscrupulous App Store developers.
sentences.zh: 存在恶意服务，可以向不择手段的 App Store 开发者大量出售虚假评级和评论。

sentences.en: Apple claims to prevent App Store fraud, but Apple seems to be about as effective at stopping fake ratings and reviews as it is at stopping scam apps from appearing in the App Store.
sentences.zh: 苹果声称要防止应用商店欺诈，但苹果在阻止虚假评级和评论方面似乎与阻止诈骗应用程序出现在应用商店方面一样有效。

sentences.en: In other words, not very effective.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，效果不太好。

blocks.html_en: In 2026, we’re long overdue for Apple to “think different” about App Store user ratings and reviews. What I see from Apple here is nothing except shameful complacency.

sentences.en: In 2026, we’re long overdue for Apple to “think different” about App Store user ratings and reviews.
sentences.zh: 到 2026 年，我们早就应该让苹果对 App Store 用户评分和评论“以不同的方式思考”。

sentences.en: What I see from Apple here is nothing except shameful complacency.
sentences.zh: 我从苹果这里看到的除了可耻的自满之外什么也没有。

Previous: No, you curate the App Store

Jeff Johnson (My apps, PayPal.Me, Mastodon)

July 29 2026

我本来可以用“App Store”来结束这篇博文的标题，但我想谈谈今天我想到的一些具体事情：App Store 用户评分和评论。 这个主题与昨天的博客文章不，你管理 App Store 相关。 尽管苹果员工在开发者发布到 App Store 之前会私下审查每个应用程序的每个版本，据说是为了确保应用程序的质量，验证它们是否按照他们声称的那样做，但苹果公司仍然依赖 App Store 用户对应用程序进行评分和评论。 您可能想知道一款经过 Apple 审核、批准的应用程序如何仍能获得一星评级。 另一方面，其中一些一星评级是不值得的、不公平的。

18 年前，当 App Store 开业时，它是 iTunes 音乐商店的翻版，旨在销售 99 美分的歌曲。 事实上，iPhone App Store 已包含在 Mac 版 iTunes 中。 这种受歌曲启发的设计给软件市场带来了许多不幸的后果，例如图表驱动的逐底竞争。 你可能会原谅苹果匆忙组建一个系统：毕竟，当iPhone本身在前一年推出时，它并不支持第三方原生应用程序。 相反，网络应用程序是史蒂夫·乔布斯（Steve Jobs）所捍卫的“甜蜜解决方案”，尽管大多数其他人对这个想法感到不满。 无论如何，那是两任苹果首席执行官之前的事了，约翰·特努斯现在升任该办公室。 随着时间的推移，App Store 得到了巨大的发展，但在许多重要方面，它仍然是 iTunes 音乐商店的旧版、构思不善的克隆，这对 App Store 用户和开发者造成了损害。

歌曲和软件市场的区别应该是显而易见的：

  1. 价格。 iTunes 音乐商店中的歌曲大多为 99 美分或接近该价格，而 App Store 中的应用程序价格差异很大。 苹果自己的 Final Cut Pro 在 Mac App Store 中的售价为 299.99 美元。
  2. 购买。 歌曲没有歌曲内购买功能。 他们都是预付款的。 尽管像我这样的一些老派开发者顽固地坚持应用程序的预付费商业模式，但应用程序商店激励应用程序内购买，并且大多数应用程序都遵循苹果的激励措施。
  3. 质量。 一首歌“只是有效”，如果由于某种原因它拒绝播放，那是苹果和 iTunes 的错，而不是音乐家在歌曲中写的“错误”。 从 iTunes 音乐商店下载的歌曲只做一件事：播放音频。 歌曲不像应用程序那样具有多种功能、选项和工作流程。 如果一首歌让你不高兴，那也不是错误。音乐主要是个人品味的问题。
  4. 支持。 软件需要开发商的技术支持。 歌曲不需要音乐家的技术支持。 您通常无法联系音乐家。 也许几十年后林戈·斯塔尔会回复你的粉丝来信。
  5. 安全。 iTunes 音乐商店没有恶意软件或诈骗。 最大的危险是露骨的歌词。 音乐家已经由唱片公司策划，因此苹果在发布歌曲之前不需要对其进行审查。 据我所知，iTunes 音乐商店不接受公众的业余提交。 相比之下，世界上任何一个不知名的人只要支付 99 美元参加苹果开发者计划就可以向 App Store 提交应用程序。

匿名众包评级和评论系统是为歌曲设计的，唯一重要的是个人音乐品味。 歌曲是娱乐性的，不是功利性的。 这个系统应用于应用程序时非常糟糕。 下面是我今天发现的一星评论——App Store 开发者必须手动检查评论，因为苹果无法向我们发送电子邮件通知，正如我在博客文章 App Store 可以为开发者改进的小方法中提到的——抱怨我的应用程序要求评级…… 与 App Store 中的大多数其他应用程序一样！

编辑：一些读者，例如《黑客新闻》（叹气），在没有使用我的应用程序的情况下，从上面的屏幕截图中假设了太多。 我发表这篇评论是因为它是最近的，而不是因为它是典型的。 事实上，这是非典型的。 我不记得还有其他人审查过我的评级请求。 总的来说，我的应用程序得到了很高的评价和好评。 在这种情况下，审核者使用“nag”一词，但我的应用程序没有 nag 屏幕。 有一个非模式按钮，不会中断您对应用程序的使用。 我在这篇博文中抱怨的是苹果的系统，而不是我自己的评论。

想象一下，如果科技新闻媒体的专业作家将此应用程序评论提交给他们的编辑以供出版。 作者可能会因无能而被解雇。 然而苹果允许这样的评论发布到应用商店。 同样在今天，一位 App Store 开发者在社交媒体上发布了他们的应用收到的功能请求一星评论的屏幕截图：

这些评论都没有谈论该应用程序的实际功能，无论它们是否有效或工作得如何。 这些评论是非理性的挑剔，选择一个狡辩并对此进行整个评论。 不知何故，基于这一因素，这些应用程序应该获得整体一星评级吗？ 根本问题在于，总体而言，App Store 用户无论从经验还是气质上都没有资格撰写软件评论。 他们是业余爱好者，而不是专业人士。 软件值得比这更好的东西。 一些App Store用户甚至出于技术支持的目的滥用审核系统，而不是联系支持人员提出问题，但实际上不可能在App Store审核和开发人员响应中与用户进行来回对话，例如，如果我需要用户提供更多信息。 该系统绝对不是为此设计的！

独立开发者无法在 App Store 中获胜。 由于我们大多不为公众所知，因此我们需要对我们的应用程序进行正面的 App Store 评级和评论来鼓励购买。 如果我们不要求所有用户进行评分，那么自发评分的人往往会不成比例地是有抱怨的用户，而不是满意的用户。 开明的用户认识到我们的困境，但也有像上面那位这样的私刑用户，他们似乎决心惩罚所有评级请求，并产生意想不到的结果，使独立开发者破产。 苹果可以通过在购买后的某个时候向 App Store 客户发送电子邮件，要求对应用程序进行评分来缓解这个问题，这样应用程序开发人员就不需要请求评论。 事实上，如果评级请求是由苹果发起的，那么苹果甚至可以禁止开发者在 App Store 中发起评级请求。 不幸的是，苹果似乎对缓解应用商店的任何问题不感兴趣。 苹果甚至不承认评级和评论系统存在问题。

您是否应该相信匿名的众包评级和评论？ 预付费应用程序的评级和评论可能大多是诚实的，尽管通常写得不好。 开发商可以撰写或购买虚假评论，但如果数量过多，成本将变得相当高。 另一方面，对于免费下载的应用程序，世界上任何人都可以对应用程序进行评分和评论。 这常常导致欺诈。 存在恶意服务，可以向不择手段的 App Store 开发者大量出售虚假评级和评论。 苹果声称要防止应用商店欺诈，但苹果在阻止虚假评级和评论方面似乎与阻止诈骗应用程序出现在应用商店方面一样有效。 换句话说，效果不太好。

到 2026 年，我们早就应该让苹果对 App Store 用户评分和评论“以不同的方式思考”。 我从苹果这里看到的除了可耻的自满之外什么也没有。

Jeff Johnson (My apps, PayPal.Me, Mastodon)
